name: Bright Outdoor Media Limited
summary: Profitable outdoor-advertising expansion is real, but weak cash realization, noncore capital allocation and a demanding dated valuation limit attractiveness. Completed latest-half-year-based annual scenarios do not meet the 15% hurdle even in the bull case. Migration remains conditional.
identity_note: Primary sources identify legal company and listing; verify any later migration before execution.
score_note: Canonical weights retained; persistent cash realization weakness CASH 3 caps GQS 5. Numeric IAS uses completed annual financing/noncore equity model with dated secondary quote and explicit uncertainty ranges.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Bright is an established outdoor-advertising operator, not an asset-light advertising annuity. FY26 profit growth and October new sites are positive, but receivables, prepaid site costs, real estate and intercorporate deposits consume capital. September 2026 reviewed results show only ₹0.5859 crore CFO against ₹11.0271 crore PAT. BQS 5.18, GQS capped 5 and conditional IAS 3.245 distinguish business progress from unattractive price economics. Reference five-year total-return IRR −2.19%, bull 9.87%, both below 15% hurdle from the dated 19 October ₹331 close. Avoid a compounder premium until cash realization and capital allocation improve; no allegation of adjudicated misconduct or certain default is made. [S1][S6][S7][S8][S95]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Bright Outdoor Media Limited, ISIN INE0OMI01019, BSE 543831/BRIGHT, BSE SME at 20 October 2026. June Board/shareholder migration proposals are not effective listing notices; the 19 October issuer release still makes BSE mainboard migration/NSE listing conditional. Official interop master confirms 21,823,166 shares and lot 375; its encoded date is not substituted for the issuer’s 24 March 2023 listing history. Annual FY26 standalone Indian GAAP/AS, no subsidiaries; September review references Ind AS 34 without a formal transition bridge in reviewed statements, a basis-wording gap rather than verified adoption. Historical statements are in rupees, converted by 10 million; latest interim is ₹ lakh, divided 100. Five synthetic years from 30 September 2026, 15% hurdle and ₹5 lakh liquidity reference. [S1][S6][S7][S10][S91]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV4/MOAT5/REV7/DUR6/CAP5/CASH 3/BAL7/EXEC6/EARN6. REV uses representative FY23–26 CAGR 18.70%, not the pandemic-trough five-year rate. CAP includes noncore/immature capital, rather than excluding poorly deployed assets. CASH 3 reflects several weak periods even after correcting known financing/deposit classifications; it is not derived from raw CFO alone. Persistent weakness caps raw GQS 5.95 at 5. R1 reflects reference IRR −2.19% less 15% hurdle; D4 recognizes severe loss under combined claims/collection stress despite a low reported-debt starting point; P3 reflects demanding valuation, L5 conditional historical capacity with lot/missing-data caveats. GOV and CAP each ±1 move BQS by ±0.32 combined and IAS by ±0.08 through Q; these small differences should not be interpreted as precise rankings. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Bright sells access to outdoor advertising sites, display execution and allied services, using owned/contracted inventory and commercial partners; it also trades/lets real estate and holds financial deposits. A commercial hoarding venture is not automatically a consolidated legal subsidiary. FY26 advertising plus printing ₹146.6162 crore versus property/rental ₹6.4103; current H1 advertising ₹70.4251 versus ₹61.8578 and property ₹0.7685 versus ₹0.6488. Site access depends on leases/tenders, municipal permissions, renewal prices and available locations. Digital screens improve scheduling and utilization possibilities but require equipment, electricity/maintenance and customer demand. Reported counts of 490 hoardings and 1300 displays use different units and must not be presented as like-for-like network growth. [S1][S2][S6][S9][S10][S12]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Longstanding advertiser/agency relationships and high-traffic Mumbai sites are meaningful operating advantages; renewals, competitive site costs and concentrated geography limit their durability. Prospectus historical top 10 customer revenue share 44.14% in FY22 and 40.47% in September 2022 is not a current concentration clearance. Graphisads combines outdoor units with government/multimedia work, while Crayons is an integrated creative/media/events agency: gross revenue and cash cycles are not directly comparable to Bright’s site portfolio. Lamar is structurally different again because of its US REIT/distribution framework. None supplies an automatic Indian SME terminal multiple. Exit 7/11/14× core EBIT are explicitly assumed sensitivity points, not contemporaneous verified peer trading averages. [S2][S14][S15][S16]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Standalone revenue FY21 ₹24.0366, FY22 ₹50.4612, FY23 ₹91.5035, FY24 ₹106.6789, FY25 ₹126.7455, FY26 ₹153.0265 crore. Pandemic-trough recovery inflates the five-year endpoint growth rate; FY23–26 CAGR 18.70% better represents the recent operating scale. FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26 PAT ₹7.1044/16.0384/19.0750/24.0467; FY23 ₹9.6164 is PBT, not PAT. H1 FY27 revenue ₹71.1936 and PAT ₹11.0271 versus ₹62.5067/₹10.0752, giving TTM ₹161.7134/₹24.9986. H1 advertising segment profit fell ₹18.1294→₹16.9120, but unallocated expenses fell ₹5.6805→₹3.0674; allocating all those expenses to advertising gives ₹12.4489→₹13.8446. Thus group profit improvement is not simply expanding segment margin. Do not annualize a monsoon half-year or trust unreconciled reported EPS. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: October 17 announcement adds 22 partner sites,104 displays and 53,898 square feet; June/July Mira-Bhayandar additions show execution, not audited future occupancy or yields. Core expansion requires deposits, prepayments, receivables and fixed digital equipment, as well as structures carried in inventory. March property stock/WIP/advances total ₹38.2801 crore and ICDs ₹8.6662; no automatic premium is assigned to these assets. September property segment net assets ₹39.1714 replace, rather than add to, that older property amount. Using total equity less only explicitly unpledged-bank proxy leaves invested capital ₹163.6286 versus ₹145.9603 crore. Consistently normalized advertising NOPAT ₹18.9017 versus ₹17.0084 yields average return 12.21% and incremental 10.72%, below a 15% hurdle. These analyst proxies retain noncore capital and do not claim audited project-level returns. New sites and digital conversion are a runway only if additional collections cover their capital cost. [S1][S5][S6][S8][S9][S11][S12]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Yogesh/Jagruti FY26 disclosed remuneration ₹0.36/0.12 crore is modest relative to PAT. However, 28 September shareholders approved authority for FY27 aggregate remuneration up to 15% of Section 198 profit; this is a ceiling, not evidence the full amount has been paid. Model separately tests a 15%-of-EBIT proxy, explicitly not the statutory calculation. Audit/IFC and bank-statement alignment conclusions are positive. The current auditor nevertheless states office 801–804 Crescent Tower/parking title remains in the predecessor proprietorship’s name; use rights are not equivalent to completed title transfer. March 2023 prospectus disclosed historical allotment/return/transfer-record and former-subsidiary consolidation deficiencies, with no proceedings then stated; no blanket current resolution is assumed. FY26 audit lists service-tax ₹32 crore and GST ₹3.19 crore appeals pending, with management disputing bundled printing treatment and ITC mismatch respectively. These are disputed exposures, not adjudicated payable losses or fraud findings.  [S1][S2][S13]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 CFO ₹3.6097 versus ₹5.0517 crore, two-year raw CFO/PAT 0.201x; capex ₹0.5530 makes reported FCF ₹3.0567. But the cash-flow presentation puts ICD advances and older long-debt repayments in operating lines. Known long-debt-repayment reclassification changes FY23 CFO −₹12.3507 to ₹3.7906, FY24−₹18.0603 to −₹17.1815 and FY25 ₹5.0517 to ₹5.4167; these are analyst diagnostics, not audited restatements. Adding FY25/FY26 ICD deployment ₹2.7212/5.9450 gives ₹8.1379/9.5547 before other property/interest differences, still weak against normalized earnings. FY26 receivables ₹78.7467 include accrued-not-due display ₹23.1460; over-six-month overdue ₹11.7031 improved from ₹16.3396, contrary evidence to a blanket deterioration claim. September CFO ₹0.5859 relied partly on ₹5.5746 security-deposit release while payables fell ₹9.3140. Its inventory/advance cash-flow split differs from BS changes by offsetting ≈₹3.665 crore, so total WC effect is not rejected solely for this reclassification. Prior-period gratuity ₹0.8624 charged to reserves and separately deducted in cash flow needs a cash/noncash bridge. FY24 comparatives were regrouped in FY25, including inventory/prepayments and a bounded ₹0.1454 crore total-assets change; no complete bridge is fabricated. Annual reported EPS 12.26/13.11 fails retrospective bonus comparison: on 2.1823166 crore shares, FY26/FY25 EPS ₹11.0189/8.7407. H1 actual arithmetic ₹5.0529, not table ₹10.25. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Dated ₹331 quote implies ₹722.3468 crore equity, about 30.04× FY26 and 28.90× TTM PAT. Model uses September cash ₹25.2906, no reported funded debt, and assumes March pledged ₹3.5544 remains unavailable; latest actual pledge split is unknown and all-FD-unavailable sensitivity is shown. Positive CC/OD bank-asset labels are not automatically reclassified as debt; a separate adverse sensitivity excludes ₹3.6585 cash and adds equal debt. Core opening ONWC ₹105.1468 excludes property net assets and assumed carried March ICD once. Base advertising sales 180/201.6/221.76/241.7184/261.0559, margin 17.5%, WC 63→58%, capex 6/6/7/7/8 and DA 1.8% fund growth explicitly. Core margin includes site/rent and bank-charge expenses; property earnings/FD interest are not capitalized again. Property 80% and ICD 70% recoverable terminal values are assumptions, not appraisals. Terminal 11× EBIT plus noncore value/cash less debt yields ₹293.8489; fixed ₹0.50 annual dividend only when cash permits gives −2.19% IRR. Bear ₹89.3078/−22.87%, bull ₹526.8328/9.87%. Base/bull need no new borrowing; bear requires ₹12.6379 not guaranteed. DCF 18% base ₹141.25 is a present-value cross-check. All FD unavailable gives −2.69% IRR; full tax loss −3.29%; additional WC 10 points −3.00%; remuneration proxy −5.10%. This is a complete conditional scenario model, not a claim that current restrictions, debt offers or future occupancy are known. [S1][S6][S13][S95]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Bear combines ad demand weakness, margins 12/10/11/12/13%, slower collections, full ₹35.19 crore disputed-tax cash loss in year 2 and 15% receivable impairment ₹12.1953 crore. The impairment reduces opening recoverable ONWC, is added back to PAT in CFO, and lowers cash realization once; it is not an extra cash expense on top of the same writeoff. Property recovered at 50%, ICD 0, no property-income double count. Terminal ₹89.31 is 73.02% below quote and assumes the modeled ₹12.64 crore financing can be obtained; failure to fund, loss of sites, adverse title developments or larger claims can worsen outcomes. Tax payment is a downside assumption, not an asserted decided liability. Base cash cushion makes a near-term solvency failure less compelling than valuation/quality risk, but does not make shares capital-protected. [S1][S2][S6]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold prices ₹1655/₹3310 require 37.97%/58.49% annual price appreciation over five years. At current shares they imply equity ₹3611.73/₹7223.47 crore. Ignoring favorable net cash/noncore offsets,11× core EBIT would require ₹328.34/₹656.68 crore EBIT, or about ₹1876/₹3752 crore sales at 17.5% margin, versus base year 5 ₹261.06. Even bull price is only 1.59× the dated quote. Bonuses do not create operating value; migration approval, awards or claimed network leadership alone cannot bridge this earnings requirement. [S1][S6][S7][S10]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: At each half-year: reconcile accrued/unbilled display income, debtor ageing and subsequent cash receipts; separate property/ICD cash from advertising cash. Obtain current ICD counterparties/security/maturity, property title/valuation and Sept segment allocation bridge. Require cash/bank confirmation identifying free, pledged, CC/OD and customer-guarantee balances; no account identifiers are republished. Verify status/amounts of tax appeals and title transfer, and actual remuneration versus authorization. Track matched-format site count, occupancy, revenue per site/digital panel and renewal costs, not mixing hoardings/displays. Confirm effective migration notice before reclassification. Historical 60 session 54 observed rows support only conditional exit capacity: low×volume proxy 5% participation ≈6.09 days observed-only,6.40 conditional zero-fill; missing 6 dates are not proven no-trade days. Lot 375 costs ₹124125; four lots ₹496500 fit illustrative budget. Actual turnover, spread/depth and complete BSE surveillance status remain unverified. [S1][S6][S7][S8][S91][S95]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: An ordinary-to-moderate-quality growing advertising business with weak aggregate cash discipline and unattractive dated valuation, rather than a demonstrated high-quality compounder. Conditional analytical ranking is supported by completed cash/financing scenarios, but is not executable investment approval. Improve the case through collections, productive site investment, transparent noncore allocation and actual financing/title/tax disclosures; do not infer safety from reported debt-free status or assume approval of a pay ceiling proves actual excess payment. Full-model review is complete with genuine evidence gaps retained. [S1][S6][S13][S95]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Read FY23–26 annuals, SEBI final prospectus,16 October reviewed H1 results, recent business/migration releases, remuneration vote and primary peer business materials. Broken issuer old PDF links were replaced by primary-file mirrors, not treated as source-exhaustion. Current segment property classification, exact ICD/pledged cash split, legal outcomes and contract level unit economics remain unavailable. Source facts, management network claims, analyst reclassifications and future assumptions are separately identified. The annual/half-year accounting-basis wording and EPS/table differences require correction but are bounded enough for conservative modeling; no fabricated clean audit assurance is offered. Models are reproducible, dated and include debt/cash/dividend/noncore bridges and downside funding. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S13]
